Alongside the physical loop we maintain a three-tier simulation ladder used for screen- ing and hypothesis generation, never as ground truth. Tier C (rigid struts with spring tendons in a rigid-body dynamics engine, roughly 0.15 s per design) ranks large design sets; Tier B (de- formable struts with explicit tendon cross-sections, seconds to tens of seconds per design) restores the tendon-stiffness sensitivity that Tier C is blind to; and Tier A (hyperelastic finite-element contact simulation, about a minute per design after meshing) captures strut buckling and self-contact for a handful of designs. The ladder applies the same SAE J211 CFC-180 filtering as the physical pipeline so simulated and measured records are processed identically. Its honest scorecard against the measured seed round is mixed and is reported as such: an intensive volumetric energy-absorption score computed at Tier C showed a strong exploratory in-sample rank as- sociation with the measured _t_180 (Spearman ρ=-0.93 across the seven mapped articles, exact two-sided permutation ρ≈0.0067; because the metric was evaluated on the seed set and candidate- metric selection was not multiplicity-adjusted, this is hypothesis- generating rather than validated predictive performance), yet the ladder’s own simulated _t_180 correlates only weakly with the mea- surement (ρ ≈0.5), rigid-strut models cannot reproduce the ob- served amplification (_t_180_\>_1 on five of eight measured articles), and simulated restitution is design-invariant where the measured rebound is not. We therefore use the ladder to prioritize candidates and probe mechanisms (for example, the mass-confound diagnosis in Section 5) while keeping every surrogate observation physical. Full engine benchmarks and the simulation-side BO study, in which the same acquisition pipeline run on the Tier-C evaluator reaches 97% of an exhaustively computed reference hypervolume while random and space-filling baselines reach 61 to 66%, are provided in the Supplementary Information. 3.6 Metal-Analog Validation. To test whether the rankings learned on the printed PLA/TPU specimens generalize beyond the as-printed polymer system, a final validation campaign re produces a subset of the _T_3-prism designs as _metal analogs_ built from hollow aluminum rods (compression members) and stainless- steel threaded cables (tension members), using the same _R_, _H_, θ, and member-diameter parameterization. Rather than fabricat- ing only the top-ranked geometries, we deliberately span the predicted performance range: a few designs the surrogate predicts to be _worst_-performing, a few mediocre, and a few _best_-performing are each built in both material systems. Comparing the mea- sured ordering of the PLA/TPU specimens against their hollow- aluminium/stainless-steel counterparts tests whether both systems preserve the same rank ordering of energy-absorption performance, which would indicate that the optimization transfers across material systems rather than overfitting to the printed polymers. We treat this as a _stringent_, _exploratory_ transfer test rather than a presumed one-to-one validation: the deformation modes, joint compliance, friction, pretension behavior, and strain-rate sensitivity all differ between the PLA/TPU and aluminum/steel systems, so agreement is not expected a priori. The rank-preservation criterion is fixed in advance as the Spearman rank-correlation coefficient ρs between the two material systems’ orderings of the primary campaign met- ric (_t_180 under the identical drop protocol), with the rebound en-ergy Ereb and, once the quasi-static extension runs, SEA reported as secondary rankings; ρs near unity would support cross-system transfer of the learned design ranking. 4 reports the planned rank-ordering comparison and Fig. 5 shows the assembled metal- analog and printed-polymer specimens for each performance tier. ## 4 Results ### 4.1 Seed-Round Measurements. ## 5 Discussion

### 5.0.1 What the seed round establishes.

The round-1 data set- tle three questions the planned-methods stage could only pose. The end-to-end pipeline runs: printed articles, hundred-drop characterizations, a fitted fully Bayesian surrogate, and a model- recommended batch on the printer within days of the last seed measurement. The measurement distinguishes the tested articles: their _t_<sub>180</sub> means span 0.169, well beyond within-session drop scat ter; whether this separation reproduces across newly printed arti- cles remains to be tested. And the physics is more adversarial than the cushioning intuition suggests: at this scale and rate, five of the eight measured prisms amplify the peak shock reaching their top vertex and only one tested article attenuated it, which sharpens the campaign question from “how much does the architecture cushion” to “which corner of the design space crosses into attenuation, and whether attenuation reproducibly incurs a rebound-score cost.”

### 5.0.2 Honest accounting of the objective stack.

We pre- registered an adversarial, data-first review of the objective choices with an external AI referee that was required to commit to its own objective set from the raw campaign files before reading ours. Its findings temper the round-1 formulation and set the round-3 revisi- sion: the rebound fraction e<sub>reb</sub> rests on a ballistic interpretation of the second contact event that has not yet been validated against syn- chronized video (a restrained-versus-unrestrained check is scheduled); the apparent _t_<sub>180</sub>-versus-rebound trade-off is driven sub- stantially by the single strongest attenuator (Spearman \(\rho=-0.39\), _p=_0.38 across the reliable articles); and per-drop standard errors are substantially smaller than the provisional 0.72% between-article CV estimated in a five-print repeatability study, and therefore un derstate article-level uncertainty. The round-3 plan therefore refits with article-level noise, treats rebound as a candidate constraint pending its validation, and reserves print capacity for replicate articles. We report this trajectory rather than presenting the round-1 choices as final because the loop is the contribution and revis ing objectives mid-campaign, with the revision criteria stated in advance, is how such loops behave in practice.

### 5.0.3 Mass as a confound and as a design variable.

Holding solid CAD mass constant did not hold printed grams constant: PLAprints at partial infill while thin TPU cables print near solid, so the seed articles span 18.50 g to 22.29 g, and among the seven mapped tested articles mass and _t_<sub>180</sub> are correlated (_r=_0.83). Printed mass is itself induced by the geometry and is strongly collinear with member dimensions (light articles _are_ the thick-strut, thin-cable corner by construction), so these seven observations cannot identify separate geometry and mass effects; a post hoc mass-adjusted

5.0.4 Relation to prior art. Relative to Pajunen et al. [11], the present work varies the geometry under an optimization loop rather than characterizing a single fabrication condition; relative to Mo et al. [17], the loop’s ground truth is physical measurement with simulation demoted to a screening ladder whose predictive reach we quantify rather than assume (Section 3.5). The measured near-unity transmission of most seed articles also caution against reading the printed-tensegrity literature’s attenuation reults as generic: the as-printed cells here are not pretensioned, and activating genuine pretension in additively manufactured tenseg rity (for example through shrink-on-treatment routes) is an open direction we deliberately scope out of the present campaign.

5.0.5 Practical considerations and path forward. TPU-PLA interface durability under repeated impact remains open: no joint failed during the repeated-drop measurement sessions, but because those sessions were not designed as controlled fatigue tests, the observation does not establish interface durability. Sensitivity to print-process covariates (the print key logs defects, humidity, and the mid-batch nozzle change for exactly this purpose) and transfer to other material pairs likewise remain open. The path forward includes the quasi-static crush characterization (Section 3.3), pretension activation, tiled multi-cell absorbers and lattices [36], and miniaturization to crutch-tip envelopes: long-term crutch use is associated with substantial upper-extremity overuse injury and ground-reaction-force impulses [62–66]; existing springloaded [67,68] and polymer-damped [69] tip designs reduce loading rate but not peak transmitted force, and recent tensegrity crutch concepts [70] and open-source 3D-printed crutch work [71] suggest a plausible translation path, with adjacent footwear and orthotic lattice studies [72–74] providing transferable design heuristics.

5.0.6 Limitations. The evidence base is a single seed round on single prints of each design (_n=_1 article per geometry; one design was printed in triplicate, which provides mass replication only, since a single article of that design appears in the reported mechanical-response table); the drop protocol probes one height, one impact surface, and axial loading only; the specimens never leave the elastic regime, so crush-energy metrics await the quasistatic campaign; per-specimen energy absorption in joules is not recoverable from the current rig (the falling-mass and displacement

channels required for a force integral are not instrumented); one tested article lacks a design mapping and one seed design’s official article assignment carries a recorded discrepancy; and all results are from a single printer, material pair, and cell topology. The metal-analog protocol (Section 3.6) and the pre-registered revision plan above are the designed responses to these limits.

## 6 Conclusions

We have presented an experiment-driven Bayesian-optimization framework for designing multi-material 3D-printed tensegrityinspired energy absorbers using PLA struts and TPU tension elements, and we have completed its first measure-and-recommend step on physical hardware; closure of the full recommend- fabricate–measure–update cycle awaits the round-2 tests. The framework parameterizes a five-variable _T_<sub>3</sub>-prism family under a constant-mass fairness projection, fabricating each candidate in a single multi-material FDM build with TPU tendons anchored inside the PLA strut ends, characterizes every article with 101 instrumented drops, and updates a fully Bayesian Gaussian-process surrogate [22,24] that recommends the next batch. In the ninedesign seed round the filtered peak-acceleration ratio spanned 0.89 to 1.06 across the eight tested articles, while within-session per- drop CVs were below 0.5% (article-level reproducibility remains under study); one tested article attenuated the peak shock under the tested condition; and the first model-recommended batch of nine designs has been generated and sent to fabrication. The workflow is a candidate for other experimentally evaluated architected structures whose constitutive response is difficult to calibrate from first principles, but transfer beyond this printer, material pair, topology, and axial impact condition remains untested.

## Sensors and calibration.

Base input: single-axis piezoelectric accelerometer on the carriage plate (1.059mV/G, full scale 9443G); top response: Dytran 3133A4 triaxial accelerometer (X/Y/Z 0.690/0.667/0.734mV/G) seated in a printed pocket at the top vertex, mounted per ISO 5348. An earlier single-axis channel was retired after range clipping. The two base-capable channels were cross-calibrated in place over fifteen co-located drops: ratio \(0.953\pm 0.001\) at CFC-180 (per-drop \(0.952\pm 0.004\)), stable across drop heights (PR #74).

## Filtering correction.

The SAE J211/1 channel-frequency-class filter used for all reported numbers is implemented from the standard’s published coefficients. An earlier in-house implementation passed the two-pass (forward-backward) corner frequency to a single-pass design, which narrows every channel class by roughly 20% (an effective CFC-144 where CFC-180 was intended); the discrepancy was identified during the analysis audit of issue #94 and corrected before the campaign numbers were produced.

## Processing pipeline.

For each capture, every channel is calibrated and CFC-filtered independently; the top-vertex magnitude \(\|\mathbf{a}_\text{top}(t)\|\) is formed from the three filtered triaxial components, and the two peaks entering _t_<sub>180</sub> are searched within a short window (approximately 1.5ms) of first contact, so the peaks need not be simultaneous. The baseline is estimated from the record tail (at healthy tower speed the mat-contact foot begins before the 2ms pre-trigger window). \(\Delta v\) is the integral of the baselined base channel over the impact pulse and doubles as the rig-health gate. Drops are discarded per the warm-up rule; remaining per-capture exclusions, the second-contact detector’s threshold and search window, the exact window bounds and filter-initialization choices, and the "stabilized mean" convention are defined in the campaign analysis code, whose archival release with a version tag is a declared submission gate; they are summarized here rather than restated numerically to avoid divergence from the code of record.

## Rig health and repair history.

Rig health is gated on the impact velocity change \(\Delta v\) recovered from the base channel; over an uninterrupted 100-drop session the \(\Delta v\) CV was 0.54% with a flat drift slope. During commissioning, two guide-rod locking pins failed and a defeated pin-park safety interlock was discovered and recommissioned; the pin-related friction produced a measurable \(\Delta v\) deficit that resolved after repair (issue #92). Approximately 3,660 instrumented drops across roughly 50 printed specimens were performed over three months of commissioning and characterization before the campaign sessions (issue #101); the campaign itself contributes over 800 clean captures to date.

### Objective provenance and adversarial review.

The objective stack evolved through a measurability review (PR #97): per-specimen crush energy in joules is not recoverable from this rig (no falling-mass or displacement channel, and the specimens stay elastic), which is why the campaign objectives are the filtered peak-acceleration ratio and the rebound energy, with quasi-static crush metrics deferred to a load-frame campaign. ## S5 Printed-Mass Model

The seed batch was projected onto constant _solid_ CAD mass (_m<sup>⋆</sup>_=30.95g), yet the articles weigh 18.50g to 22.29g, because PLA struts print at partial infill (15% grid, two walls) while thin TPU cables print near solid, and the PLA-to-TPU volume split swings widely across the design box. A two-stage calibrated model closes this gap (PR #102, `bo/t3\_prism\_mass\_model.py`): analytic member volumes are corrected to rendered-solid grams (one factor per material), and rendered-solid grams are mapped to weighed grams through a wall-plus-infill term in the as-printed strut diameter (fitted infill 23.6%, wall 1.18mm, TPU factor 0.744). The model’s residual standard deviation is 0.378g. For context, the three available prints of design 08 have a sample standard deviation of 0.457g; three prints of one geometry are insufficient to establish a general process repeatability limit. Inverting it inside the projection allows rounds to hold _printed_ grams constant with no slicer in the loop. Two round-2 recommendation sets exist in the record and must not be conflated: the batch actually sliced and sent to the printer was generated before this correction, under the seed round’s solid-mass projection, with the mass-aware objectives and each recommendation’s predicted printed mass reported; a subsequently regenerated set applies the constant-printed-mass projection (target 20.23g, the reference article’s weight) and is the working proposal for round 3. The repository’s suggestion CSV at the branch head is the regenerated (constant-printed-mass) set.

## S6 Simulation Fidelity Ladder

The screening ladder of the main text was assembled and benchmarked in PR #33. Tier C is a MuJoCo rigid-strut, spring-tendon model (about 0.15s per design with CFC-180 filtering); PyBullet and PyChrono equivalents were benchmarked and demoted (the PyBullet bare-prism peak is contact-dominated and design-invariant). Tier B is a Newton/Warp XPBD model with deformable struts and explicit tendon cross-sections (seconds to tens of seconds per design), which restores the tendon-stiffness sensitivity Tier C lacks. Tier A is a PolyFEM incremental-potential-contact hyperelastic model of the welded PLA/TPU prism (about a minute per run), which captures strut buckling and self-contact.

Documented blind spots carried into any use of the ladder: Tier-C peak acceleration is floor- contact dominated and nearly flat across cable stiffness; the apparent strut-diameter leverage in unconstrained sweeps is largely a mass/contact confound (it shrinks about seventeenfold under a constant-mass sweep); the twist variable is not consumed by the Tier-C regime plumbing; rigid- strut models cannot reproduce the measured amplification (_t_<sub>180</sub>_\>_1 on five of eight bench articles, while simulated _t_<sub>180</sub> cannot exceed about 1); and simulated restitution is design-invariant where the measured rebound is not. Against the measured seed round (_n_=7 mapped articles), an<tbc>

4

============================================================

============================================================

<tbc>intensive volumetric energy-absorption score computed at Tier C showed a strong exploratory in- sample rank association with measured _t_<sub>180</sub> (Spearman \(\rho=-0.93\), exact two-sided permutation _p_≈0.0067; hypothesis-generating rather than validated prediction, since the metric was evaluated on the seed set without multiplicity adjustment), while the ladder’s own simulated _t_<sub>180</sub> reaches only \(\rho\approx 0.5\).

A simulation-side closed-loop study using the same Ax/BoTorch pipeline on the Tier-C evaluator (ten independent Sobol-seeded repeats of 36 designs each) reached 97.1% of an exhaustively computed reference-front hypervolume, versus 80.4% for compass search and 60 to 66% for random, Latin-hypercube, and Sobol baselines, with the smallest seed-to-seed spread; this motivates the budget-matched baseline comparison planned for the physical campaign but is not evidence about the physical loop itself.

## S7 Metal-Analog Validation Plan

A final validation campaign rebuilds a subset of the _T_<sub>3</sub>-prism designs as metal analogs (hollow aluminum rods for the compression members and stainless-steel threaded cables for the tension members) using the same _R_, _H_, \(\theta\), and member-diameter parameterization as the printed PLA/TPU specimens. To probe transfer across material systems rather than only confirming the optimum, the selected designs deliberately span the predicted performance range: representatives the surrogate predicts to be worst-, mid-, and best-performing are each built in both material systems and characterized under the identical drop protocol of Section S4. Agreement between the measured PLA/TPU ranking and the hollow-aluminum/stainless-steel ranking on the primary campaign metric _t_<sub>180</sub> (reported in the main-text metal-analog validation table and figure, with rebound energy and, later, quasi-static SEA as secondary rankings) indicates that the optimization generalizes beyond the as-printed polymers.

 511→\subsection{Design Parameterization}
 512→\label{sec:methods:parameterization}
 513→
 514→We parameterize a family of tensegrity-inspired unit cells via four
 515→groups of design variables. For the working $T_3$-prism prototype that
 516→defines the initial BO search space (Section~\ref{sec:methods:bo}),
 517→only the first two groups are active and all of their variables are
 518→\emph{continuous}; the connectivity-topology and tiling groups are
 519→held fixed for this prototype and are listed here as planned
 520→extensions of the design family:
 521→\begin{itemize}
 522→  \item \textbf{PLA compression members.} Strut diameter $d_s$ and
 523→    length $\ell_s$, with the slenderness ratio $\ell_s / d_s$ bounded
 524→    away from buckling-dominated regimes.
 525→  \item \textbf{TPU tension elements.} Cross-sectional area $A_t$ (or
 526→    equivalent diameter $d_t$ for circular cross-sections).
 527→  \item \textbf{Connectivity topology (future extension).} Selected
 528→    from a discrete set of candidate unit cells (e.g.,
 529→    truncated-tetrahedral, prism-based, and octahedral variants); when
 530→    activated, the design vector would encode this as a categorical
 531→    choice. It is held fixed at the $T_3$ prism for the present
 532→    campaign.
 533→  \item \textbf{Unit-cell tiling (future extension).} Number of cells
 534→    $N_x \times N_y \times N_z$ and the orientation of each cell
 535→    relative to the impact direction; held fixed at a single cell here.
 536→\end{itemize}
 537→\todo{Specify exact manufacturing-feasibility constraints once
 538→finalized; the connectivity-topology categorical encoding is deferred
 539→until that variable is activated beyond the $T_3$ prism.}
 540→
 541→\paragraph{Working prototype} The first instance of this family used
 542→to validate the fabrication and test pipeline is a three-strut,
 543→$T_3$-prism-inspired cell scaled to a $\sim$50\,mm bounding box. As
 544→implemented in the BO harness, this working prototype exposes five
 545→continuous design variables (base radius $R$, cell height $H$, twist
 546→angle $\theta$, a single strut diameter $d_s$, and a single cable
 547→(tendon) diameter $d_t$) over the ranges listed in
 548→Table~\ref{tab:design-vars}; the cable diameter $d_t$ is treated as a
 549→\emph{continuous} variable on $[3.0, 5.5]$\,\si{mm} rather than a
 550→discrete set. Under the prism's $D_3$ symmetry all struts share one
 551→diameter and all cables share one diameter, so the present
 552→parameterization uses a single strut-diameter axis and a single
 553→cable-diameter axis (two member-diameter axes), leaving room to relax
 554→to per-orbit (saddle, top, bottom) or fully per-member diameters once
 555→the individual orbits have been characterized.\todo{Cite the
 556→heterogeneous-parameters Edison LITERATURE\_HIGH brief
 557→(\texttt{5191cf4d}) on $D_3$-symmetric vs.\ fully-per-member
 558→parameterization.} The joint diameter $d_j$ is held fixed at
 559→\SI{7.0}{mm} rather than optimized: it sets the printed strut-end cage
 560→that houses the internal cable anchors
 561→(Section~\ref{sec:methods:fabrication}), so it is constrained primarily by the
 562→TPU-tendon outlet count and the dual-nozzle clearance rather than by
 563→energy-absorption performance, and fixing it keeps the anchor geometry
 564→constant across specimens so that the five optimized variables are not
 565→confounded by joint-strength changes; relaxing $d_j$ is deferred to a
 566→follow-on joint-design study. Figure~\ref{fig:printed-prototypes}
 567→shows the parametric CAD model alongside an as-printed prototype of this
 568→working $T_3$ prism.
 569→
 570→\paragraph{Constant-mass projection and printability screens} Because
 571→cell mass varies severalfold across the raw design box, an
 572→unconstrained search would partly reward designs for carrying more
 573→material rather than for their architecture. Every candidate is
 574→therefore projected onto a constant material budget before printing:
 575→the design is uniformly rescaled (all dimensions except the twist
 576→angle) until its solid CAD mass
 577→$\rho_{\mathrm{PLA}} V_{\mathrm{PLA}} + \rho_{\mathrm{TPU}}
 578→V_{\mathrm{TPU}}$ equals $m^{\star} = \SI{30.95}{g}$, the solid mass
 579→of the reference prism, converged to within \SI{0.15}{g} on rendered
 580→geometry. Two printability screens are evaluated on the projected
 581→geometry and recorded as flags rather than hard rejections: a
 582→cylindrical build envelope $\pi R^2 H \le \SI{250}{cm^3}$ and the
 583→\SI{3.0}{mm} TPU self-bridging floor on the as-projected cable
 584→diameter (the projection can scale a nominally feasible cable below
 585→the floor; the two seed designs where this occurred both exhibited
 586→tendon stringing defects, consistent with the screen). The choice of a
 587→\emph{solid-mass} budget has a documented limitation discussed in
 588→Section~\ref{sec:discussion}: PLA struts print at partial infill
 589→while thin TPU cables print near solid, so as-printed masses still
 590→ranged from \SIrange{18.50}{22.29}{g} across the seed batch; a
 591→calibrated printed-mass model that closes this gap is described in
 592→the Supplementary Information.

 679→\subsection{Multi-Material Fabrication}

 682→Specimens are fabricated on a multi-material FDM printer using PLA for
 683→the rigid struts and TPU for the soft tension elements.

 688→wrapping the struts in a continuous TPU skin, the current design anchors
 689→the TPU tension elements \emph{inside} the ends of each PLA strut: the

 696→wrapping~\cite{ye2023multimaterial}: here a soft TPU core is captured within

 698→precedent rather than as validation of the present junction. \todo{Quantitatively

 709→OpenSCAD study (anchor-bulb, dovetail, TPU-sleeve overmold,
 710→eyelet-loop, and TPU-rebar variants); the working prototype uses a
 711→dovetail joint (Design~B) with an anchor-bulb backup (Design~A) for
 712→sensitivity studies, with a captive TPU core routed inside the PLA
 713→shell to keep the soft tendon protected from layer-line failure at
 714→the strut-to-cable transition. The full five-design comparison and the
 715→selected junction are detailed in the Supplementary Information.\todo{Cite the

 722→generation is disabled and supports are painted manually in the

 789→\subsection{Experimental Characterization}
 790→\label{sec:methods:testing}
 791→
 792→\paragraph{Drop-tower fixture} The primary characterization is
 793→repeated drop-weight impact on a Lansmont Model~23 shock test system.
 794→The printed specimen rides upright on the carriage plate, which is
 795→raised \SI{60}{in} (\SI{1.524}{m}) along guide rails and released; the
 796→plate lands on a single \SI{0.5}{in} Shore 60~OO polyurethane cushioning
 797→sheet, which shapes the landing into a single sharp base pulse of
 798→roughly \SI{1.6}{ms} duration. This impact-surface configuration was
 799→selected by a blinded crossover experiment over three candidate mat
 800→arrangements, and unlike a felt stack it does not measurably compact
 801→over hundred-drop sessions. Rig health is monitored continuously
 802→through the impact velocity change $\Delta v$ recovered from the base
 803→accelerometer: over an uninterrupted 100-drop characterization session
 804→the $\Delta v$ coefficient of variation was 0.54\% with no drift, and
 805→every campaign session is gated on $\Delta v$ remaining at the healthy
 806→tower baseline. One drop takes roughly \SI{42}{s}, so a full
 807→101-drop specimen characterization completes in about ninety minutes.
 808→
 809→\paragraph{Instrumentation and signal processing} A single-axis
 810→piezoelectric accelerometer on the carriage plate records the base
 811→input and triggers the acquisition; a triaxial accelerometer (Dytran
 812→3133A4) seated in a printed pocket at the specimen's top vertex records
 813→the transmitted response. The two base-capable channels were
 814→cross-calibrated in place over fifteen co-located drops (ratio
 815→$0.953 \pm 0.001$ at matched filtering), and the transducer settings
 816→are archived with the data. Signals are captured at
 817→\SI{1.25}{MHz} over a \SI{100}{ms} record with a \SI{2}{ms}
 818→pre-trigger. All channels are low-pass filtered with the SAE~J211/1
 819→channel-frequency-class (CFC) filters~\citep{saej211}, implemented from
 820→the standard's published coefficients with the two-pass corner
 821→frequency handled explicitly (a common implementation shortcut narrows
 822→the passband by roughly 20\%, which we identified and corrected before
 823→the campaign; all reported numbers use the corrected filter). CFC-180
 824→is the reporting class for peak metrics, with CFC-1000 retained as a
 825→higher-bandwidth diagnostic.
 826→
 827→\paragraph{Per-specimen objectives} Each drop session contributes 101
 828→valid captures to the stabilized statistics (103 for one article,
 829→autv5r), counted after the first two drops of each session are
 830→discarded as warm-up. Each session yields two objectives, each reported as a stabilized mean
 831→with the per-drop scatter quoted as one standard deviation; the
 832→standard error of the mean is what enters the surrogate's noise model
 833→(Section~\ref{sec:methods:bo}):
 834→\begin{equation}
 835→  \begin{aligned}
 836→    t_{180} &\;=\; \frac{\max_t\,\lVert \mathbf{a}_{\mathrm{top}}(t)\rVert_{\mathrm{CFC180}}}
 837→                        {\max_t\,\lvert a_{\mathrm{base}}(t)\rvert_{\mathrm{CFC180}}},\\
 838→    E_{\mathrm{reb}} &\;=\; e_{\mathrm{reb}}\, m\, g\, h,
 839→    \qquad
 840→    e_{\mathrm{reb}} \;=\; \frac{g\, t_{\mathrm{second}}}{2\,\Delta v},
 841→  \end{aligned}
 842→  \label{eq:objectives}
 843→\end{equation}
 844→where $t_{180}$ is the CFC-180 \emph{filtered peak-acceleration
 845→ratio}: the peak magnitude of the triaxial top-vertex response over
 846→the peak base input within the impact window. We deliberately do not
 847→call this quantity a transmissibility: the two peaks need not be
 848→simultaneous and a single transient drop cannot produce the averaged
 849→frequency-response function that the standards-defined transmissibility
 850→requires, so $t_{180}$ is a filter-class-specific ranking metric rather
 851→than a standards quantity, and SAE~J211/1 is cited here only for the
 852→impact-channel filtering. Values above unity indicate the structure
 853→amplifies the peak shock reaching its top vertex; values below unity
 854→indicate attenuation. $E_{\mathrm{reb}}$ is a \emph{provisional
 855→mass-weighted rebound score} with units of energy (millijoules per
 856→drop): the dimensionless rebound fraction $e_{\mathrm{reb}}$ is
 857→recovered from the ballistic timing of the top vertex's post-impact
 858→hop~\citep{bernstein1977listening} ($t_{\mathrm{second}}$ is the time
 859→to the second contact event and $\Delta v$ the measured base velocity
 860→change), and it is scaled by each article's own weighed mass $m$ and
 861→the drop height $h$. Two interpretive caveats are deliberate. The
 862→ballistic reading of the second contact event has not yet been
 863→validated against synchronized video, and $\Delta v$ is the base
 864→plate's velocity change rather than a demonstrated incident relative
 865→velocity, so $e_{\mathrm{reb}}$ is a rebound-timing score rather than
 866→a coefficient of restitution; and because a strict restitution reading
 867→would scale returned kinetic energy as the \emph{square} of a velocity
 868→ratio, $E_{\mathrm{reb}}$ is a mass-aware ranking score that penalizes
 869→designs (and grams) that throw more motion back at the payload, not a
 870→measured rebound energy. The score is used as the round-1 second
 871→objective and is slated to become a constraint once validated
 872→(Section~\ref{sec:discussion}). Using the mass-weighted form rather
 873→than the bare fraction keeps the objective mass-aware: equal fractions
 874→on articles of different printed mass are not equivalent outcomes for
 875→a payload. Ringdown descriptors (the
 876→fitted natural frequency $f_n \approx$ \SIrange{300}{470}{Hz} and, where
 877→the exponential fit passes an $r^2 \ge 0.85$ gate, a damping ratio
 878→$\zeta$) are recorded per drop as print-health and prestress
 879→diagnostics~\citep{ashwear2014natural} but are not campaign objectives.
 880→The within-session per-drop CV of $t_{180}$ is 0.17 to 0.48\%. These
 881→values describe repeated drops of the same physical article and do
 882→not estimate print-to-print or geometry-level repeatability; serial
 883→dependence among drops may also make
 884→$s/\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{drops}}}$ optimistic. For the single article
 885→measured in two sessions, the two session means differed by 0.13\%;
 886→this isolated re-test does not estimate cross-session
 887→reproducibility. Figure~\ref{fig:dropcurve} illustrates the mechanism-oriented
 888→presentation we adopt for the processed traces, linking features of the
 889→measured signal to the structural events that produce them.
 890→
 891→\paragraph{Planned quasi-static extension} The drop test loads the
 892→specimens in their elastic regime (the crush lasts 1 to \SI{3}{ms} and
 893→the article recovers), so crush-energy metrics such as specific energy
 894→absorption (SEA) and compaction efficiency are not recoverable from
 895→these captures by any reprocessing. A quasi-static compression
 896→campaign on a benchtop load frame (BYU CB~123 Instron, with a
 897→low-range load cell appropriate to the expected cell stiffness)
 898→is planned to supply the complementary crush metrics
 899→\begin{equation}
 900→  \mathrm{SEA} \;=\; \frac{1}{m}\!\int_{0}^{\delta_d}\! F(\delta)\,
 901→  \mathrm{d}\delta,
 902→  \qquad
 903→  \eta_c \;=\; \frac{\int_{0}^{\delta_d}\! F(\delta)\,\mathrm{d}\delta}{F_{\max}\,\delta_d},
 904→\end{equation}
 905→with the densification displacement $\delta_d$ taken at the maximum of
 906→the energy-absorption efficiency curve and $F_{\max}$ the peak force
 907→within $[0,\delta_d]$, following the canonical cellular-solid
 908→treatments~\citep{gibson1997cellular, avalle2001characterization,
 909→tan2005dynamic, michailidis2011establishment} and mirroring the
 910→quasi-static protocol of Pajunen et~al.~\citep{pajunen2019design}.
 911→These metrics are reported as a complementary characterization of
 912→selected designs rather than as objectives of the drop-tower campaign.
 913→Slip resistance and traction at the specimen-to-floor interface,
 914→governed by the tip geometry rather than the internal architecture,
 915→follow ISO 11334-4~\citep{iso11334-4} for walking-aid tips and are out
 916→of scope for the present axial-impact study.

 947→\subsection{Experiment-Driven Bayesian Optimization Loop}
 948→\label{sec:methods:bo}
 949→
 950→The optimization loop maintains a Gaussian-process (GP) surrogate over
 951→the design space defined in
 952→Section~\ref{sec:methods:parameterization}. After each round of
 953→physical experiments, the surrogate is refit and an acquisition
 954→function is maximized to recommend the next batch of designs to
 955→fabricate. The campaign is posed as a two-objective minimization:
 956→simultaneously minimize the filtered peak-acceleration ratio $t_{180}$
 957→and the per-drop rebound score $E_{\mathrm{reb}}$ of
 958→Eq.~\eqref{eq:objectives}. Both objectives serve the same payload:
 959→$t_{180}$ bounds the peak shock it feels during the impact, and
 960→$E_{\mathrm{reb}}$ penalizes the motion thrown back into it afterward.
 961→The seed data show an apparent trade-off driven substantially by the
 962→single strongest attenuator; at seven mapped articles it is not
 963→statistically resolved (Spearman $\rho = -0.39$, $p = 0.38$;
 964→Section~\ref{sec:discussion}), which is why the rebound axis is slated
 965→to become a constraint rather than an objective once validated.
 966→Implementation
 967→uses the Ax platform~\citep{pmlr-v293-olson25a} over
 968→BoTorch~\citep{balandat2020botorch}, with noisy expected hypervolume
 969→improvement (qNEHVI)~\citep{daulton2021nehvi} as the multi-objective
 970→acquisition. The working $T_3$-prism search space is fully continuous
 971→(the five variables of Table~\ref{tab:design-vars}), so no categorical
 972→encoding is required; the mixed-search-space constructions
 973→of~\citep{garridomerchan2020dealingwithcategorical} and the BOCS
 974→combinatorial baseline~\citep{baptista2018bocs} remain the route for
 975→the future connectivity-topology categorical rather than part of the
 976→current loop. The input-noise-robust acquisition of Daulton
 977→et~al.~\cite{daulton2022robust} and the evolution-guided constrained
 978→variant of Low et~al.~\cite{low2024evolution} are held in reserve as
 979→contingencies.
 980→
 981→\paragraph{Surrogate and noise model} The surrogate is the fully
 982→Bayesian sparse axis-aligned subspace model
 983→(SAASBO)~\citep{eriksson2021saasbo}: a Mat\'ern-5/2 kernel with
 984→automatic relevance determination whose length scales carry strong
 985→sparsity-inducing priors and are marginalized by Markov-chain Monte
 986→Carlo rather than point-estimated. We retain SAASBO even though the
 987→dimensionality is modest because marginalizing the hyperparameters
 988→tends to improve uncertainty quantification at the very small sample
 989→sizes of physical campaigns; the fitted model is audited each round
 990→with leave-one-out cross-validation and length-scale-based sensitivity
 991→diagnostics against a standard single-task GP with the same kernel
 992→(Section~\ref{sec:results}). Inputs are normalized to the unit cube
 993→and outputs standardized. Observation noise is supplied per
 994→observation as a fixed variance: for $t_{180}$ the squared standard
 995→error of the stabilized mean,
 996→$\sigma_t^2 = s_{\mathrm{drop}}^2 / n_{\mathrm{drops}}$, and for the
 997→rebound score the drop-scatter term plus the propagated
 998→print-to-print mass scatter,
 999→$\sigma_E^2 = \sigma_{E,\mathrm{drops}}^2 +
1000→(\partial E_{\mathrm{reb}}/\partial m)^2 \sigma_m^2$ with
1001→$\sigma_m = \SI{0.457}{g}$ measured from the one design printed in
1002→triplicate. The estimand this noise model implies is the response of
1003→the tested article, not of a freshly printed article at the same
1004→design: an independent adversarial review
1005→(Section~\ref{sec:discussion}) argues the decision-relevant target is
1006→the latter, for which a provisional article-level noise scale of
1007→0.72\% CV, estimated from five prints (14
1008→to 44 times the per-drop standard error), should replace the per-drop
1009→terms; the round-3 refit adopts that correction. SAASBO is the
1010→prespecified round-1 surrogate; we make no claim that it outperforms
1011→a standard single-task GP at this dimensionality and sample size, and
1012→the budget-matched calibration comparison remains a pending audit
1013→(Section~\ref{sec:results}).
1014→
1015→\paragraph{Mass treatment} Because the constant \emph{solid}-mass
1016→projection does not hold printed grams constant
1017→(Section~\ref{sec:methods:parameterization}), printed mass correlates
1018→with the shape variables in the seed round ($r = 0.83$, $n = 7$,
1019→dominated by the lightest article, against $t_{180}$). The loop
1020→therefore makes mass explicit rather than pretending it away: the
1021→rebound objective is expressed in absolute millijoules using each
1022→article's weighed mass, so added grams are re-penalized through the
1023→energy they deliver back to the payload, while $t_{180}$ deliberately
1024→stays a ratio because payload peak acceleration is a damage criterion
1025→that does not scale with specimen mass. The objective surrogates take
1026→the five design coordinates of Table~\ref{tab:design-vars} as their
1027→inputs; printed mass is attached as a separately modeled
1028→\emph{tracking metric}, so the model learns as-printed mass as a
1029→function of the design coordinates and every recommendation reports a
1030→predicted printed mass (the diagnostic refit behind
1031→Fig.~\ref{fig:sensitivity} additionally includes printed mass as a
1032→sixth input, precisely to probe this confound). A calibrated
1033→printed-mass model that would let future rounds hold \emph{printed}
1034→grams constant is described in the Supplementary Information.
1035→
1036→\paragraph{Budget and seeding} The seed round is an $n = 9$ Sobol
1037→draw with a recorded seed over the five-variable box, printed together
1038→with the fixed reference prism (S0). Optimization proceeds in
1039→sequential batches of $q = 9$ prints, sized to one build-plate
1040→generation cycle; the first model-recommended batch (Ax trials 10
1041→to 18) is reported in Section~\ref{sec:results}. All random seeds,
1042→the full experiment state, and the recommendation tables are recorded
1043→per round; full computational reproducibility (the exact processing
1044→pipeline and model settings) is carried by the campaign code, whose
1045→archival release is a declared submission gate rather than a solved
1046→item. Escalation to
1047→trust-region BO (TuRBO)~\citep{eriksson2019turbo} is planned only if
1048→per-member-diameter extensions push the design space well beyond the
1049→present regime; a single-objective log-Expected-Improvement
1050→run~\citep{ament2023logei} on $t_{180}$ is retained as a baseline for

1057→\subsection{Simulation Screening Ladder}
1058→\label{sec:methods:simulation}
1059→
1060→Alongside the physical loop we maintain a three-tier simulation ladder
1061→used for screening and hypothesis generation, never as ground truth.
1062→Tier~C (rigid struts with spring tendons in a rigid-body dynamics
1063→engine, roughly \SI{0.15}{s} per design) ranks large design sets;
1064→Tier~B (deformable struts with explicit tendon cross-sections,
1065→seconds to tens of seconds per design) restores the tendon-stiffness
1066→sensitivity that Tier~C is blind to; and Tier~A (hyperelastic
1067→finite-element contact simulation, about a minute per design after
1068→meshing) captures strut buckling and self-contact for a handful of
1069→designs. The ladder applies the same SAE~J211 CFC-180 filtering as the
1070→physical pipeline so simulated and measured records are processed
1071→identically. Its honest scorecard against the measured seed round is
1072→mixed and is reported as such: an intensive volumetric
1073→energy-absorption score computed at Tier~C showed a strong
1074→exploratory in-sample rank association with the measured $t_{180}$
1075→(Spearman $\rho = -0.93$ across the seven mapped articles, exact
1076→two-sided permutation $p \approx 0.0067$; because the metric was
1077→evaluated on the seed set and candidate-metric selection was not
1078→multiplicity-adjusted, this is hypothesis-generating rather than
1079→validated predictive performance), yet the
1080→ladder's own simulated $t_{180}$ correlates only weakly with the
1081→measurement ($\rho \approx 0.5$), rigid-strut models cannot reproduce
1082→the observed amplification ($t_{180} > 1$ on five of eight measured
1083→articles), and simulated restitution is design-invariant where the
1084→measured rebound is not. We therefore use the ladder to prioritize
1085→candidates and probe mechanisms (for example, the mass-confound
1086→diagnosis in Section~\ref{sec:discussion}) while keeping every
1087→surrogate observation physical. Full engine benchmarks and the
1088→simulation-side BO study, in which the same acquisition pipeline run
1089→on the Tier-C evaluator reaches 97\% of an exhaustively computed
1090→reference hypervolume while random and space-filling baselines reach
1091→61 to 66\%, are provided in the Supplementary Information.
1092→
1093→\subsection{Metal-Analog Validation}
1094→\label{sec:methods:validation}
1095→
1096→To test whether the rankings learned on the printed PLA/TPU specimens
1097→generalize beyond the as-printed polymer system, a final validation
1098→campaign reproduces a subset of the $T_3$-prism designs as
1099→\emph{metal analogs} built from hollow aluminum rods (compression
1100→members) and stainless-steel threaded cables (tension members), using
1101→the same $R$, $H$, $\theta$, and member-diameter parameterization.
1102→Rather than fabricating only the top-ranked geometries, we
1103→deliberately span the predicted performance range: a few designs the
1104→surrogate predicts to be \emph{worst}-performing, a few
1105→\emph{mediocre}, and a few \emph{best}-performing are each built in
1106→both material systems. Comparing the measured ordering of the
1107→PLA/TPU specimens against their hollow-aluminum/stainless-steel
1108→counterparts tests whether both systems preserve the same
1109→rank ordering of energy-absorption performance, which would indicate
1110→that the optimization transfers across material systems rather than
1111→overfitting to the printed polymers. We treat this as a
1112→\emph{stringent, exploratory} transfer test rather than a presumed
1113→one-to-one validation: the deformation modes, joint compliance,
1114→friction, pretension behavior, and strain-rate sensitivity all differ
1115→between the PLA/TPU and aluminum/steel systems, so agreement is not
1116→expected a priori. The rank-preservation criterion is fixed in advance
1117→as the Spearman rank-correlation coefficient $\rho_s$ between the two
1118→material systems' orderings of the primary campaign metric ($t_{180}$
1119→under the identical drop protocol), with the rebound energy
1120→$E_{\mathrm{reb}}$ and, once the quasi-static extension runs, SEA
1121→reported as secondary rankings; $\rho_s$ near unity would support
1122→cross-system transfer of the learned design ranking.
1123→Table~\ref{tab:metal-validation} reports the planned rank-ordering
1124→comparison and Fig.~\ref{fig:metal-validation} shows the assembled
1125→metal-analog and printed-polymer specimens for each performance tier.

1177→800 clean captures within a project-wide history of roughly 3{,}660
1178→instrumented drops. Table~\ref{tab:seed-results} reports the
1179→stabilized objectives. Three findings frame the round. First, the
1180→measured $t_{180}$ spans 0.893 to 1.062: five of eight tested articles
1181→\emph{amplify} the peak shock reaching the top vertex (means above
1182→unity), two sit marginally below unity (0.997 and 0.980), and one
1183→tested article (the print of Sobol spec~01, the thick-strut,
1184→thin-cable, high-twist corner of the batch) had a mean $t_{180}$ of

1312→expected behavior of a
1313→five-variable space observed at seven mapped articles rather than as
1314→evidence for or against variable relevance; the diagnostics are
1315→refreshed every round.
1316→
1317→\begin{figure}[t]
1318→  \centering
1319→  \includegraphics[width=0.92\linewidth]{../figures/bo/t3-prism-bo-round1-feature-importance.png}
1320→  \caption{Round-1 SAASBO length-scale diagnostics per objective
1321→    (normalized inverse length scales; median over MCMC draws,
1322→    interquartile whiskers; inputs are the five design variables plus
1323→    printed mass; the horizontal axis, labeled ``share of model
1324→    sensitivity'' in the plot, is this normalized inverse-length-scale
1325→    diagnostic). No input separates decisively from the equal-share
1326→    line (dashed) at seven mapped articles, and these are
1327→    prior-sensitive model diagnostics, not evidence of variable
1328→    relevance.}
1329→  \label{fig:sensitivity}
1330→\end{figure}
1331→
1332→\begin{figure}[t]
1333→  \centering
1334→  \includegraphics[width=0.92\linewidth]{../figures/bo/t3-prism-bo-round1-loocv.png}
1335→  \caption{Round-1 leave-one-out cross-validation of the SAASBO
1336→    surrogate: predicted versus observed values with model error bars
1337→    for both objectives.}
1338→  \label{fig:loocv}
1339→\end{figure}
1340→
1341→\subsection{Later-Round Placeholders}
1342→Round-2 outcomes, the budget-matched baseline comparison, the
1343→SAASBO-versus-standard-GP calibration audit, and the replicate-article
1344→repeatability study are pending data and will complete this section.
1345→\todo[inline,color=red!30]{Populate once round-2 articles are tested:
1346→(1) predicted-versus-measured landing plot and updated Pareto front;
1347→(2) hypervolume versus experiment count against a budget-matched
1348→random/Sobol baseline; (3) SAASBO versus standard single-task GP
1349→calibration comparison on the accumulated data; (4) replicate-article
1350→repeatability table (the round-3 plan reserves print capacity for
1351→replicates per the adversarial objective review).}
1352→
1353→% =============================================================================
1354→\section{Discussion}
1355→\label{sec:discussion}
1356→% =============================================================================
1357→
1358→\paragraph{What the seed round establishes} The round-1 data settle
1359→three questions the planned-methods stage could only pose. The
1360→end-to-end pipeline runs: printed articles, hundred-drop
1361→characterizations, a fitted fully Bayesian surrogate, and a
1362→model-recommended batch on the printer within days of the last seed
1363→measurement. The measurement distinguishes the tested articles: their
1364→$t_{180}$ means span 0.169, well beyond within-session drop scatter;
1365→whether this separation reproduces across newly printed articles
1366→remains to be tested.
1367→And the physics is more adversarial than the cushioning intuition
1368→suggests: at this scale and rate, five of the eight measured prisms
1369→\emph{amplify} the peak shock reaching their top vertex and only one
1370→tested article attenuated it, which sharpens the campaign question
1371→from ``how much does the architecture cushion'' to ``which corner of
1372→the design space crosses into attenuation, and whether attenuation
1373→reproducibly incurs a rebound-score cost.''
1374→
1375→\paragraph{Honest accounting of the objective stack} We
1376→pre-registered an adversarial, data-first review of the objective
1377→choices with an external AI referee that was required to commit to
1378→its own objective set from the raw campaign files before reading
1379→ours. Its findings temper the round-1 formulation and set the round-3
1380→revision: the rebound fraction $e_{\mathrm{reb}}$ rests on a ballistic
1381→interpretation of the second contact event that has not yet been
1382→validated against synchronized video (a restrained-versus-unrestrained
1383→check is scheduled); the apparent $t_{180}$-versus-rebound trade-off
1384→is driven substantially by the single strongest attenuator (Spearman
1385→$\rho = -0.39$, $p = 0.38$ across the reliable articles); and
1386→per-drop standard errors are substantially smaller than the
1387→provisional 0.72\% between-article CV estimated in a five-print
1388→repeatability study, and therefore understate article-level
1389→uncertainty. The round-3 plan
1390→therefore refits with article-level noise, treats rebound as a
1391→candidate constraint pending its validation, and reserves print
1392→capacity for replicate articles. We report this trajectory rather
1393→than presenting the round-1 choices as final because the loop is the
1394→contribution and revising objectives mid-campaign, with the revision
1395→criteria stated in advance, is how such loops behave in practice.
1396→
1397→\paragraph{Mass as a confound and as a design variable} Holding
1398→solid CAD mass constant did not hold printed grams constant: PLA
1399→prints at partial infill while thin TPU cables print near solid, so
1400→the seed articles span \SIrange{18.50}{22.29}{g}, and among the seven
1401→mapped tested articles mass and $t_{180}$ are correlated
1402→($r = 0.83$). Printed mass is itself induced by the geometry and is
1403→strongly collinear with member dimensions (light articles \emph{are}
1404→the thick-strut, thin-cable corner by construction), so these seven
1405→observations cannot identify separate geometry and mass effects; a
1406→post hoc mass-adjusted regression would be unstable and would
1407→estimate a different, direct-effect quantity. We therefore report
1408→mass as a confounded tracking variable rather than attributing the
1409→association to mass or geometry. The mass-aware rebound objective and
1410→the tracked mass metric are the round-1 compromise, and the
1411→calibrated printed-mass model (Supplementary Information) enables a
1412→constant-printed-mass projection that compares geometries at
1413→approximately fixed printed mass in later rounds.
1414→
1415→\paragraph{Relation to prior art} Relative to Pajunen
1416→et~al.~\cite{pajunen2019design}, the present work varies the geometry
1417→under an optimization loop rather than characterizing a single
1418→fabrication condition; relative to Mo
1419→et~al.~\cite{mo2023accelerated}, the loop's ground truth is physical
1420→measurement with simulation demoted to a screening ladder whose
1421→predictive reach we quantify rather than assume
1422→(Section~\ref{sec:methods:simulation}). The measured near-unity
1423→transmission of most seed articles also cautions against reading the
1424→printed-tensegrity literature's attenuation results as generic: the
1425→as-printed cells here are not pretensioned, and activating genuine
1426→pretension in additively manufactured tensegrity (for example through
1427→shrink-on-treatment routes) is an open direction we deliberately
1428→scope out of the present campaign.
1429→
1430→\paragraph{Practical considerations and path forward} TPU-PLA
1431→interface durability under repeated impact remains open: no joint
1432→failed during the repeated-drop measurement sessions, but because
1433→those sessions were not designed as controlled fatigue tests, the
1434→observation does not establish interface durability. Sensitivity to
1435→print-process covariates (the print key logs defects, humidity, and
1436→the mid-batch nozzle change for exactly this purpose) and transfer to
1437→other material pairs likewise remain open. The path forward
1438→includes the quasi-static crush characterization
1439→(Section~\ref{sec:methods:testing}), pretension activation, tiled
1440→multi-cell absorbers and lattices~\citep{sabounizawadzka2024experimental},
1441→and miniaturization to crutch-tip envelopes: long-term crutch use is
1442→associated with substantial upper-extremity overuse injury and
1443→ground-reaction-force impulses~\citep{requejo2005upperextremitykinetics,
1444→rasouli2020walkingassistanceusing, manocha2021injuriesassociatedwith,
1445→brasilbarrosdasilva2022painmappingand,
1446→dozono2015peripheralneuropathiesin}; existing
1447→spring-loaded~\citep{segura2007mechanicsofambulation,
1448→zhang2011biomechanicalevaluationof} and
1449→polymer-damped~\citep{macgillivray2016theinfluenceof} tip designs
1450→reduce loading rate but not peak transmitted force, and recent
1451→tensegrity crutch concepts~\citep{gu2026tensegritycrutches} and
1452→open-source 3D-printed crutch
1453→work~\citep{mottaghi2025opensource3dprintable} suggest a plausible
1454→translation path, with adjacent footwear and orthotic lattice
1455→studies~\citep{wang2025porouslatticestructure,
1456→zhang2024pressurereducingdesignof,
1457→janarthanan2024additivemanufacturingof} providing transferable design
1458→heuristics.
1459→
1460→\paragraph{Limitations} The evidence base is a single seed round on
1461→single prints of each design ($n = 1$ article per geometry; one
1462→design was printed in triplicate, which provides mass replication
1463→only, since a single article of that design appears in the reported
1464→mechanical-response table); the drop protocol probes one height, one
1465→impact surface,
1466→and axial loading only; the specimens never leave the elastic regime,
1467→so crush-energy metrics await the quasi-static campaign; per-specimen
1468→energy absorption in joules is not recoverable from the current rig
1469→(the falling-mass and displacement channels required for a force
1470→integral are not instrumented); one tested article lacks a design
1471→mapping and one seed design's official article assignment carries a
1472→recorded discrepancy; and all results are from a single printer,
1473→material pair, and cell topology. The metal-analog protocol
1474→(Section~\ref{sec:methods:validation}) and the pre-registered
1475→revision plan above are the designed responses to these limits.
1476→
1477→% =============================================================================
1478→\section{Conclusions}
1479→\label{sec:conclusions}
1480→% =============================================================================
1481→
1482→We have presented an experiment-driven Bayesian-optimization framework
1483→for designing multi-material 3D-printed tensegrity-inspired energy
1484→absorbers using PLA struts and TPU tension elements, and we have
1485→completed its first measure-and-recommend step on physical hardware;
1486→closure of the full recommend--fabricate--measure--update cycle
1487→awaits the round-2 tests. The framework
1488→parameterizes a five-variable $T_3$-prism family under a constant-mass
1489→fairness projection, fabricates each candidate in a single
1490→multi-material FDM build with TPU tendons anchored inside the PLA
1491→strut ends, characterizes every article with 101 instrumented drops,
1492→and updates a fully Bayesian Gaussian-process
1493→surrogate~\citep{balandat2020botorch, eriksson2021saasbo} that
1494→recommends the next batch. In the nine-design seed round the filtered
1495→peak-acceleration ratio spanned 0.89 to 1.06 across the eight tested
1496→articles, while within-session per-drop CVs were below 0.5\%
1497→(article-level reproducibility remains under study); one tested
1498→article attenuated the peak shock under the tested condition; and the
1499→first model-recommended batch of nine designs has been generated and
1500→sent to fabrication. \todo{Add the round-2 headline (predicted versus
1501→measured, hypervolume gain over the budget-matched baseline) once the
1502→batch is tested.} The workflow is a candidate for other experimentally
1503→evaluated architected structures whose constitutive response is
1504→difficult to calibrate from first principles, but transfer beyond this
1505→printer, material pair, topology, and axial impact condition remains
1506→untested.

{"code": "import pandas as pd, numpy as np, scipy.stats as st, re, pathlib, collections, math
r=pd.read_csv('/workspace/t3-prism-bo-batch-drop-results.csv')
m=r.dropna(subset=['mass_g']).copy()
# compute manuscript checks
m['E_mJ']=m.e_rebound_mean*m.mass_g*9.80665*1.524*1000/1000 # g conversion and mJ cancel numerically
print(m[['specimen','t180_mean','t180_sd','mass_g','e_rebound_mean','E_mJ']].to_string(index=False))
print('t range', r.t180_mean.min(),r.t180_mean.max(),r.t180_mean.max()-r.t180_mean.min())
print('CV% range',100*(r.t180_sd/r.t180_mean).min(),100*(r.t180_sd/r.t180_mean).max())
print('mass Pearson',st.pearsonr(m.mass_g,m.t180_mean))
print('omit 6lhxfy',st.pearsonr(m.loc[m.specimen!='6lhxfy','mass_g'],m.loc[m.specimen!='6lhxfy','t180_mean']))
print('mass corr Fisher CI', st.pearsonr(m.mass_g,m.t180_mean).confidence_interval(.95))
print('tradeoff Spearman t vs E',st.spearmanr(m.t180_mean,m.E_mJ))
# Pareto minimizing both
pareto=[]
for i,row in m.iterrows():
    dom=((m.t180_mean<=row.t180_mean)&(m.E_mJ<=row.E_mJ)&((m.t180_mean<row.t180_mean)|(m.E_mJ<row.E_mJ))).any()
    if not dom: pareto.append(row.specimen)
print('pareto',pareto)
# exact permutation p for spearman -0.93 possible rank coefficient n7 values
import itertools
rho_target=-0.93
# possible exact rhos / p for rank vectors 1..7
base=np.arange(7)
rhos=[]
for perm in itertools.permutations(base):
    rhos.append(st.spearmanr(base,perm).statistic)
rhos=np.array(rhos)
for val in sorted(set(np.round(rhos,8)), key=lambda x: abs(x-rho_target))[:3]:
    p=(np.abs(rhos)>=abs(val)-1e-12).mean()
    print('possible rho',val,'exact two-sided p',p,'count',sum(np.isclose(rhos,val)))
# citation keys source vs bib
tex=pathlib.Path('/workspace/manuscript-body.tex').read_text()
bib=pathlib.Path('/workspace/references.bib').read_text()
cites=[]
for x in re.findall(r'\\cite\w*\{([^}]+)\}',tex): cites += [k.strip() for k in x.split(',')]
keys=re.findall(r'@\w+\{\s*([^,]+),',bib)
print('cited unique',len(set(cites)),'bib keys',len(keys),'missing keys',sorted(set(cites)-set(keys)))
print('uncited bib',len(set(keys)-set(cites)))
# duplicate DOI and malformed types
entries=re.split(r'(?=@\w+\{)',bib)
dois=[]
for e in entries:
    km=re.match(r'@\w+\{\s*([^,]+),',e)
    dm=re.search(r'doi\s*=\s*\{([^}]+)',e,re.I)
    if km and dm: dois.append((dm.group(1).lower().strip(),km.group(1)))
print('duplicate DOI',[(d,ks) for d,ks in collections.defaultdict(list).items()])
dd=collections.defaultdict(list)
for d,k in dois: dd[d].append(k)
print([(d,ks) for d,ks in dd.items() if len(ks)>1])
print('article with booktitle',[(re.match(r'@\w+\{\s*([^,]+),',e).group(1),) for e in entries if e.startswith('@article') and 'booktitle' in e])", "display_text": "Recomputing reported statistics and auditing citation-key integrity"}

# Bibliographic Quality Problems in `/workspace/references.bib`

---

## 1. Wrong Entry Type (`@article` declared as conference paper, or vice versa)

| Key | Line | Problem |
|-----|------|---------|
| `vespignani2018design` | 361 | Declared `@article` but has a `booktitle` field (IROS 2018 conference paper). Should be `@inproceedings`. |
| `garridomerchan2020dealingwithcategorical` | 722 | Declared `@inproceedings` but `booktitle = {Neurocomputing}` — Neurocomputing is a journal, not a conference. Should be `@article` with `journal = {Neurocomputing}`. |
| `davami2019dynamicenergyabsorption` | 757 | Declared `@misc` but has full journal metadata (`journal`, `volume`, `pages`, `doi`). Should be `@article`. Also uses non-standard field `issue` (should be `number`). |
| `frazier2018tutorial` | 133 | Declared `@article` with `journal = {arXiv preprint arXiv:1807.02811}`. Should be `@misc` or `@unpublished`. |
| `zhang2021bo` | 218 | Declared `@article` with `journal = {arXiv preprint arXiv:2107.12809}`. Should be `@misc` or `@unpublished`. |
| `ament2023sustainable` | 269 | Declared `@article` with `journal = {arXiv preprint arXiv:2310.18288}`. Should be `@misc` or `@unpublished`. |
| `edelstein2019canescrutchesand` | 510 | Declared `@article` but the source is a book chapter ("Atlas of Orthoses and Assistive Devices, pages 377–382"). Should be `@incollection`. |

---

## 2. Journal Field Containing Volume/Pages/Date (Malformed `journal` Field)

The following entries (all from the Edison crutch-tip literature block, lines 478–690) embed volume, page numbers, and/or dates directly inside the `journal` field instead of using separate `volume`, `pages`, `number`, and `year` fields. This will render incorrectly in any BibTeX style.

### MANUSCRIPT (14 pages)

The dual Roman-numeral columns are almost certainly a LaTeX two-column numbering artefact and will confuse referees.
- **Author footnotes:** Five authors are listed; Hill and Baird carry both "†‡" and a superscript "1" (Corresponding Author). The footnote symbol "1" conflicts visually with reference citation numbers. The footnote text ("¹Corresponding Author. August 22, 2026") appears at the bottom of the left column in a small font — the date stamp is unusual and may need to be removed before submission.
- **Typography:** The abstract is set in italic throughout (correct for JMD style), but the keyword line uses a mix of roman "Keywords:" and italic body — consistent with style but worth confirming against journal template.
- **Header:** "Journal of Mechanical Design" (left) and "PREPRINT / 1" (right) — the dual journal/preprint branding is intentional but should be confirmed as acceptable.

**Page 2**
- **Line numbering:** Arabic line numbers continue cleanly in the left margin; right-column numbers (122–189) are present and aligned. No glitches observed.
- **References:** In-text citations [1,2], [3–5], [6–10] etc. are properly formatted with hyperlinks (blue). No issues.
- **Typography:** Section heading "2 Background" and subsection "2.1 Tensegrity-Inspired Architectures for Energy Absorption." are correctly bold/italic. No clipping.

**Page 3 (Fig. 1)**

The Bayesian Optimization inset (top centre) is small (~3 cm wide); axis labels ("f(x)", "x") and the legend text ("True model", "Noisy observation", "Surrogate model") are legible at normal reading distance but will be marginal in print at reduced size.

**Page 4 (Table 1, Fig. 2)**

The caption confirms: *"Curves are synthetic and impulse-consistent… to be regenerated from the campaign captures. Generated by scripts/figures/mechanistic_data_figure_example.py."*

**Page 8 (Table 4, Fig. 5) — CRITICAL ISSUES**
- **Table 4 — Placeholder:** Caption reads ***"Placeholder (data pending)."*** All data cells in the PLA/TPU rank and Al/SS rank columns contain only dashes (–). This is an entirely empty results table. Not submission-ready.

**Page 11 (Fig. 7)**

Axis labels ("Filtered peak-acceleration ratio t₁₈₀", "Rebound energy to payload (mJ per drop, lower is better)") are readable. Data point labels (print IDs) are legible. The blue Pareto-front line and orange diamond markers are visually distinct.

**Page 12 (Figs. 8–9)**
- **Fig. 8:** Two-panel horizontal bar chart (SAASBO length-scale diagnostics). Bars and whiskers are readable; axis label "Share of model sensitivity" is present. The figure is moderately small but legible. The caption is detailed and correctly explains the normalised inverse-length-scale interpretation.
- **Fig. 9:** Two-panel scatter plot (leave-one-out cross-validation). Points with error bars are clear; MAPE and Pearson r values are annotated on the plots. Legible at this size.
- **References [23]–[57]:** Continue in two columns. Formatting is consistent. Some arXiv preprint entries (e.g., [38]) have "Unknown journal, 2025" as the venue — this should be resolved before submission.
- **Reference [38]:** Listed venue is "Unknown journal, 2025" — a clear metadata error that needs correction.

**Page 13 (References continued)**
- **References [58]–[74]:** Continue cleanly. No formatting anomalies.
- **Large empty space:** The bottom ~40% of the page is blank after reference [74]. This is normal for a reference list ending mid-page, but combined with the placeholder figures, it signals the paper is substantially incomplete.
- **Line numbers:** Run to 1067 then stop — consistent with end of body text.

**Page 14 (List of Figures / List of Tables)**
- **List of Figures:** All 9 figures listed with page numbers. Figures 4 and 5 are listed with their placeholder/synthetic-data captions verbatim, making the incomplete status visible in the ToC.
- **List of Tables:** All 5 tables listed. Table 4 caption includes "Placeholder (data pending)" in the list — again visible to referees.
- **Typography:** Italic figure titles (Figs. 4, 5) are correctly rendered in the list.

---

### SUPPLEMENTARY (5 pages)

**SI Page 1 (S1 Joint-Design Study)**
- **Placeholder figure — CRITICAL:** Figure S1 box contains only italic text: *"Placeholder: joint-design variants and the selected dovetail/anchor-bulb junction (import figures from PR #39 / PR #35)."* No actual image is present. The caption below the box is written as if the figure exists.
- **Typography:** SI title is set in a large serif font (Computer Modern), different from the main manuscript's sans-serif style — this is a style mismatch between SI and main document that may need reconciling.

**SI Page 2 (S3 Print Key — Table S1)**

- **Note on Design 08:** Three entries for Spec 08 (dea4ls, bag26v, ghmj4y) are present with a note about the discrepancy — this is correctly flagged but may confuse referees without the surrounding context.

**SI Page 5 (S7 Metal-Analog Validation Plan)**

Caption is written as if the figure exists.
